*Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says she has not spoken with Elon Musk but is open to working with him after he described her as “quite moderate” and predicted she would be “fine” as governor.*

• *Musk:* Hinojosa acknowledged his significant business interests in Texas and said cooperation must benefit Texans.
• *Political Identity:* Asked whether she is a moderate, Hinojosa rejected ideological labels, saying, “If I had to label myself, I'd call myself an economic populist.”
• *Corporate Influence:* She argued that corporate interests have corrupted both political parties and called for leaders who prioritize constituents over corporate pressure.
• *Economic Priorities:* Hinojosa said Texas can maintain a strong business community, but its economy must serve residents first.

Lumentum *($LITE)* CEO Michael Hurlston defended its planned $115B all-stock merger with Marvell *($MRVL)* after shares plunged 42% and 45%, respectively, since Oct. 28, acknowledging shareholder frustration but citing strong AI demand.

• *Deal Outlook:* Announced Nov. 2, the merger is expected to close in H1 2028. The $115B figure represented Lumentum’s implied enterprise value at announcement.
• *Growth Driver:* Hurlston sees the shift from copper to fiber-optic connections inside AI data centers as a major opportunity, with no slowdown in Lumentum’s demand.
• *Investor Concerns:* Both stocks have suffered from merger skepticism and broader AI valuation pressure. Hurlston acknowledged, “We’ve got work to do with our shareholders.”
• *Upcoming Catalysts:* Marvell’s Dec. 1 earnings, the merger’s S-4 filing and Lumentum’s next earnings report could help rebuild investor confidence.
• *Financial Strength:* Lumentum’s latest quarterly revenue more than doubled year over year, beating expectations. Hurlston said both businesses are performing strongly.
